Hi Whiteout, IF,

I've read thru the compression book and the video several times and I'm still not grasping the difference between compression and a flag.

In the video the definition of compression is taking out the last decision point and its orders. That I understand and can follow on the chart taking out each supply/demand area and seeing what has been consumed and what hasn't.

Where I'm stuck is between a flag and compression as a flag to me indicates price may continue to the price projection from the flag.

Maybe I'm harping on this needlessly but to me until I can understand it fully I'm always going to be unsure and have doubts about what I'm seeing.

If I spot a bull flag (and by that I mean a defined rectangle but skewed on an angle) then I do the measuring thing with the pole and extend it out from the break to get an idea of how far price will move. If this occurs just before a supply area and indicates that price may move deep or thru the supply then I am very wary about going short.

If I see price narrowing into a wedge/funnel type shape then I figure that is compression and I am happy to trade from the appropriate level.

When I watch LF's video to me I'm seeing a flag (rectangle skewed on an angle) where he is saying its compression into the start of the supply zone. To me I would be hesitant to go short even tho price is moving into daily supply as by the flag price projection it could almost all the way into the zone.

When watching the video fast forward to 6 min 30 sec and watch from there and the area I have as a flag is referred to as compression.

I have also attached a chart showing the H4 chart with what I see as compression and what I see as a flag pattern.

I feel a bit silly for not being able to understand the difference and appreciate your patience while I grasp the concept.

I hope I have explainded things clearly enough.

کتاب فشردگی و ویدئوش را چند بار خوانده و دیده‌ام و هنوز تفاوت فشردگی و فلگ را نگرفته‌ام.

در ویدئو تعریف فشردگی این است که آخرین نقطهٔ تصمیم و سفارش‌هایش مصرف می‌شوند. این را می‌فهمم و می‌توانم روی چارت دنبالش کنم: هر ناحیهٔ عرضه/تقاضا را جدا برمی‌دارم و می‌بینم چه چیزی مصرف شده و چه چیزی نه.

جایی که گیر کرده‌ام بین فلگ و فشردگی است، چون به نظرم فلگ نشان می‌دهد قیمت ممکن است تا برآورد قیمت حاصل از فلگ ادامه پیدا کند.

شاید بی‌دلیل روی این نکته پافشاری می‌کنم، ولی تا وقتی کامل نفهممش، همیشه نسبت به آنچه می‌بینم نامطمئن و دچار شک خواهم بود.

اگر یک فلگ صعودی ببینم (منظورم یک مستطیل مشخص اما کج و مورب است) آن کار اندازه‌گیری با دکل را انجام می‌دهم و آن را از محل شکست امتداد می‌دهم تا بفهمم قیمت چقدر ممکن است حرکت کند. اگر این دقیقاً پیش از یک ناحیهٔ عرضه رخ دهد و نشان دهد قیمت ممکن است عمیق یا از داخل عرضه رد شود، در فروش گرفتن خیلی محتاط می‌شوم.

اگر ببینم قیمت به شکل گُوِه/قیف باریک می‌شود، آن را فشردگی می‌دانم و با خیال راحت از سطح مناسب معامله می‌کنم.

وقتی ویدئوی LF را می‌بینم، برای من یک فلگ است (مستطیلی کج و مورب) در حالی که او می‌گوید این فشردگی به‌سوی شروع ناحیهٔ عرضه است. برای من، فروش گرفتن مرددکننده است، حتی با اینکه قیمت به‌سوی عرضهٔ روزانه می‌رود، چون با برآورد قیمت فلگ تقریباً می‌توانست تا ته ناحیه برود.

وقتی ویدئو را به 6 دقیقه و 30 ثانیه می‌رسانم و از آنجا نگاه می‌کنم، همان ناحیه‌ای که من فلگ می‌دانستم را فشردگی می‌نامد.

چارتی هم ضمیمه کرده‌ام که چارت H4 را با آنچه من فشردگی می‌بینم و آنچه الگوی فلگ می‌بینم نشان می‌دهد.

کمی احساس می‌کنم که نفهمیدن این تفاوت ابلهانه است و از حوصله‌ات در درک این مفهوم سپاسگزارم.

امیدوارم به‌قدر کافی واضح توضیح داده باشم.

Yes, I don't have any stats on it either but was just going off what I've seen in general about price projections from different patterns.

When I saw how this site was laid out I made a mental note to just go thru things one step at a time. Over the past few days I've really focused on looking for CP in every chart and time frame I pull up. As with all things our ability to judge the context of situation will assist our outcomes.

I'm glad I just focused on this one thing as I feel I have a much better understanding of it now so a big thanks to Whiteout and If and all those associated with getting this site up and running.

Now that I revisit this example I think the overriding thing was a) understanding what was going on inside the flag which is compression and what it's effects are b) knowing where and how strong the supply zone is c) understanding the context of the situation to trade in direction which has the most probable outcome.

Compression

بله، من هم هیچ آماری روی آن ندارم، فقط بر اساس آنچه عموماً دربارهٔ برآورد قیمت الگوهای مختلف دیده‌ام حرف می‌زنم.

وقتی دیدم این سایت چطور چیده شده، با خودم قرار گذاشتم قدم‌به‌قدم پیش بروم. چند روز گذشته واقعاً روی پیدا کردن CP در هر چارت و هر تایم‌فریمی که باز می‌کنم تمرکز کرده‌ام. مثل همه‌چیز، توانایی ما در تشخیص بافت موقعیت به نتیجه‌مان کمک می‌کند.

خوشحالم که فقط روی همین یک چیز تمرکز کردم، چون حس می‌کنم حالا خیلی بهتر درکش می‌کنم؛ پس تشکر بزرگ از Whiteout و If و همهٔ کسانی که در راه‌اندازی این سایت نقش داشتند.

حالا که دوباره به این مثال نگاه می‌کنم، فکر می‌کنم مهم‌ترین نکته‌ها این‌ها بود: a) فهمیدن اینکه داخل فلگ چه می‌گذرد — همان فشردگی — و اثراتش چیست b) دانستن اینکه ناحیهٔ عرضه کجاست و چقدر قوی است c) فهمیدن بافت موقعیت برای معامله در جهتی که محتمل‌ترین نتیجه را دارد.

Here I will post my homework about compression.

In this first chart, I saw a lot of points of compression, but it seems that the only properly called CP is the fourth one. The three first are flags. The fifth one is a triangle or a pennant.

CP is a reversal pattern, while flags are continuation patterns. But it seems they share their nature, that is the consumption of orders while at the same time price is taked to the desire level, cleaning the way through for the next movement.

In this chart, why price has to pole to the level, instead of compressed all the way up? In the CP example (the main one, in the center of the chart) we could see how price is taken down, breaking the most recent lows, creating a pinbar that lets the shorts trapped, giving them fuel till the Supply target level. ttfreitas wrote: Thanks, Mel! With respect to the comment that you made about price compressing to the upside before reaching Demand: why does that indicate that price will brake through demand?

TT,

Here, price did bounce from the demand level, but in wich fashion? It bounced up in a compressed way. Since we also had a previous demand level that got broken (see chart), you know that you have a decison that have been made there.

In other words, we have a demand level but also a previous decision point that had been made right above it. Since price traded up to the decision point in a compressed way, we can expect that it will bounce back down from this decision point. If it bounce back down like it did, you also have to take into consideration the fact that the demand (that I pointed out) isn't fresh anymore... We can not know 100% that there are no buy orders left there anymore, untill this demand breaks to the downside.

Now, fresh demand and supply zones is another topic,I believe it's up to each trader to decide for him/herself wether he/she wants to trade every possible unfresh zones or not.

Does that makes sence to you?

A broken supply or demand level is also a zone (very important) so before searching for any compression on a chart, maybe it would be beter to look for the the supply and demand zones that are above and bellow current price, then look to see if ther are "fresh" or not and only after finding your s/d zones you can look for compression in order to make a decision. If a supply or demand zone has been tested several times, you know that the zone weakens by every revisits, so looking at how price behaves around the zones is smethig very important too.

Hope that makes sence, Best, Mel

Nice explaination Ucego!

Cp is all about price taking the pockets of Supply (while going down)and the pockets of Demand (while going up) in order to clear the orders.

1)About your first point. I would say if you see compression on a higher TF, then you have CP on this timeframe. You can have cp on a higher TF and clean s/d levels on a small TF...

2) Yes, if you see that there was pockets of supply or demand where price pulled back.

3) You always have to look at the bigger picture that has been paint. I wouldn't look for cp just in the middle of a chart. If you see a clean fresh demand level and there is cp wile price goes down to this demand then this would be a very good sign of a potential reversal Up at the demand level.

However, if you see an unfresh demand level, that has been tested several times and you see cp while price goes down, you will still have to look at your chart to see if price will like to break the demand or just bounce back up.

But Cp is Cp... Price thinks ahead of time. If price cleared the pockets of supply while going down and price broke the demand than the cp that was made there will still be valid, only not for the imediate term but probably for later...

Best, Mel

CP تمامش دربارهٔ این است که قیمت جیب‌های عرضه را (در مسیر پایین آمدن) و جیب‌های تقاضا را (در مسیر بالا رفتن) بردارد تا سفارش‌ها را پاک کند.

1) دربارهٔ نکتهٔ اولت. می‌گویم اگر فشرده‌سازی را در تایم‌فریم بالاتر ببینی، در همان تایم‌فریم CP داری. می‌شود در تایم‌فریم بالاتر CP داشت و در تایم‌فریم کوچک سطوح S/D تمیز...

2) بله، اگر ببینی جیب‌های عرضه یا تقاضایی بوده که قیمت به آن‌ها پولبک زده.

3) همیشه باید تصویر بزرگ‌تری را که نقاشی شده ببینی. من وسط چارت به دنبال CP نمی‌گردم. اگر یک سطح تقاضای تمیز و دست‌نخورده ببینی و در حالی که قیمت به سمت این تقاضا می‌رود CP وجود داشته باشد، این نشانهٔ خیلی خوبی از یک برگشت احتمالی به بالا در سطح تقاضاست.

اما اگر سطح تقاضای دست‌خورده‌ای ببینی که چند بار تست شده و در حین پایین رفتن قیمت CP هم ببینی، باز باید چارتت را نگاه کنی تا ببینی قیمت تقاضا را می‌شکند یا فقط از آن بالا می‌پرد.

اما CP همان CP است... قیمت از قبل فکر می‌کند. اگر قیمت در مسیر پایین آمدن جیب‌های عرضه را پاک کرده باشد و بعد تقاضا را بشکند، CP‌ی که آنجا ساخته شده باز هم معتبر است؛ فقط نه برای بازهٔ نزدیک، بلکه احتمالاً برای بعد...

Hi Oedipus, I think you are on the right track.

Compression is basically accumulation of orders or distribution of orders, depending which way the market is going. So if we are heading to a supply area and the big guys want to have a bulk of orders to sell with ready for when the supply zone is hit, they will keep knocking price back down whilst it is climbing, creating dips, so that the small guys buy the dips, and this allows the big guys to filter their sell orders into the market as there is now someone on the other side to buy them. If they didn't create this price dynamic then they would get awful fills and lose money.

Having all of these sell orders already in the market for when they reach the supply zone means that the one last order that shoots price down probably gets quite a bad fill, but it doesn't matter because they already have lots of other sell orders sat in the market which will be gathering a nice profit.

This is just my understanding of it, I might be wrong - I'd get some clarification from more senior members before you take this as how it really works.

سلام Oedipus، به نظرم در مسیر درستی هستی.

فشردگی اساساً انباشت سفارش‌ها یا توزیع سفارش‌هاست، بسته به اینکه بازار به کدام سمت می‌رود. پس اگر به سمت ناحیهٔ عرضه می‌رویم و بزرگ‌ها می‌خواهند حجم زیادی سفارش فروش آماده داشته باشند برای لحظه‌ای که ناحیهٔ عرضه زده می‌شود، مرتب قیمت را در حین بالا رفتن پایین می‌زنند و افت می‌سازند تا آدم‌های کوچک در آن افت‌ها بخرند؛ این اجازه می‌دهد بزرگ‌ها سفارش‌های فروششان را در بازار فیلتر کنند، چون حالا کسی آن طرف هست که آن‌ها را بخرد. اگر این دینامیک قیمتی را نمی‌ساختند، پر شدن سفارش‌هایشان فاجعه بود و پول از دست می‌دادند.

داشتن همهٔ این سفارش‌های فروش از قبل در بازار برای لحظهٔ رسیدن به ناحیهٔ عرضه یعنی آن یک سفارش آخری که قیمت را به پایین شلیک می‌کند احتمالاً پر شدن بدی می‌گیرد، اما مهم نیست، چون آن‌ها از قبل کلی سفارش فروش دیگر در بازار دارند که سود خوبی جمع می‌کنند.

این فقط برداشت من است، ممکن است اشتباه باشد — پیش از اینکه این را به عنوان روش واقعی کار قبول کنی، از اعضای باتجربه‌تر توضیح بگیر.

So the reason that the qm works isn't that the big boys have orders left there but it's because they've built up a huge short position that they haven't yet closed. Price rally's into the second high, (lots of buying by novices) when it gets there the big boys unload driving price to the floor.

پس دلیل اینکه QM کار می‌کند این نیست که بزرگ‌ها سفارش‌هایی آنجا جا گذاشته‌اند، بلکه این است که یک پوزیشن فروش خیلی بزرگ ساخته‌اند که هنوز نبسته‌اند. قیمت به سمت سقف دوم رالی می‌کند (خرید زیاد از سوی تازه‌کارها)؛ وقتی به آنجا می‌رسد، بزرگ‌ها خالی می‌کنند و قیمت را به کف می‌برند.

Just to check I understand it:

I'm reading the Red explanationof what compression is, and its difference from a flag. This is what I understand, on a bull trend:

1.- Compression is price rising to supply, but spiking south to fill small pockets of demand orders. Why? because: 1.1.- This small pockets of demand helps price to reach supply 1.2.- The way down is cleared of demand orders allowing price to make a fast big drop when it reaches supply. This clearing of orders is what we call consumption. 1.3.- Big money starts to sell slowly to this demand orders. So through compression big money finds also liquidity to fill their big orders. (?) 2.- Compression is a reversal signal, because is showing that price is clearing the way for this reversal ("PRICES THINK AHEAD OF TIME").

3.- Flag is price going down, stopping momentum on a bull trend, but spiking north for: 3.1.- Clean the supply orders so price could continue its way up. Consumption again. 3.2.- Take the price to a better demand level to have cheaper price before continue the move up. Why would we want compression? so price is able to make large moves once it hits our zone of choice. If we are looking to sell at supply we would hope that the demand zones are consumed beneath so it can fall for good r:r. Vice versa for buying.

همه‌چیز را باکس کن و برچسب بزن (روی چارت، کاغذ یا در ذهن) HTF = LTF :)

If it's useful for you, I tried to put what I understand CP is on here: www.acegazette.com/en/community/ace-foru...n.html?start=25#6391

On a word, CP when price is going up is price spiking down to consumed the demand orders. So when price reaches supply, there aren't demand orders that stop the price in its way down.

This is, I think, a good example of CP: www.acegazette.com/media/kunena/attachments/208/nu_cp3.png Price goes up from demand to supply, spiking south on the way, so consuming all the small demand orders. When price reaches supply it drop fast because the way is clean.

Other good example: www.acegazette.com/media/kunena/attachments/208/nu_cp5.png Keep an eye on how price goes up and down, filling every new demand zone, so consuming all the orders there are. When arrives to supply, it drops.

And other example: www.acegazette.com/media/kunena/attachments/208/nu_cp.png from demand to supply, consuming small demand orders, and when it reach supply, big fast drop

Hey Sunny,

Yes,buying the price compressing into Demand and vice versa for Supply is right. However, you have to look at the whole picture imo. Deciding to place a trade based only on Compression is not wise. If you see a fresh, untested Supply or Demand level but also compression while price arrives at it will add extra confluence to the trade for sure. But if for example you see an unfresh Supply or Demand level and you see compression while price arrives to it than you'll have to look at price action too imo. So everything has to be seen in it's own context.

I hope this will help. Best, Mel

Adam.

For better understanding of compression, you should ask yourself: why should I care for compression. So it is better to begin with a clear definition: A Compression is when price move away from a level (Supply or Demand) while clearing the orders flows on its way.

Exp. if price move away from demand, a compression price action would be clearing more demand on it way up to supply.

Why should you care about it? Because when price is back to the compressed area you can assume there are less order flows against the move. so back to the example, now when price hit supply and turn back toward last demand, you can assume it will show less buying power against this move.

So now you know why you need it, find PA that clears orders in a way that when price is back - it be more likely to go through fairly easy.

Here is how I would mark CP areas on your chart.

برای اینکه فشردگی را بهتر بفهمی، باید از خودت بپرسی: چرا اصلاً باید به فشردگی اهمیت بدهم. پس بهتر است با یک تعریف روشن شروع کنیم: فشردگی وقتی است که قیمت از یک سطح (عرضه یا تقاضا) دور می‌شود و در مسیرش جریان سفارش‌ها را پاک می‌کند.

مثلاً اگر قیمت از تقاضا دور شود، یک PA فشردگی در مسیر بالا رفتنش به سمت عرضه، تقاضای بیشتری را پاک می‌کند.

چرا باید به آن اهمیت بدهی؟ چون وقتی قیمت به ناحیهٔ فشرده‌شده برمی‌گردد، می‌توانی فرض کنی جریان سفارش کمتری خلاف حرکت وجود دارد. پس برگردیم به مثال: حالا وقتی قیمت به عرضه می‌خورد و به سمت آخرین تقاضا برمی‌گردد، می‌توانی فرض کنی قدرت خرید کمتری خلاف این حرکت نشان می‌دهد.

حالا که می‌دانی چرا لازمش داری، PA‌ای پیدا کن که سفارش‌ها را طوری پاک کند که وقتی قیمت برمی‌گردد، احتمال بیشتری باشد که راحت از آن رد شود.

من نواحی CP را این‌طور روی چارت تو علامت می‌زنم.

This is my first attempt on a technical analysis of S&D. Also this is a first time I put into writing any kind of technical analysis regarding FX.

Homework Compression Part 1 LTF 15M

1. As PA moves between the supply and demand zones in this case there is a lot of compression

2. Buy orders get filled in on the retest of the demand zone and there is a effortless 40 pip rise do to previous CP

3. Not enough serious sell orders are found on the 4th retest of the supply zone and a bullish flag forms right below the supply line, the price breaks out of the flag and through the supply zone for another 50 pips.

4. As the price tests the former supply line, now a support it forms a bear flag and breaks effortlessly down 30 pips do to previous CP.

5. Again the price starts to wonder in between the supply and demand zones in mayor compression until it manages to enter the demand zone, pick up enough orders to reach the now many times tested and twice broken supply zone.

6. From here it is a fairly easy ride down with not much resistance found at the demand zone as it breaks it and heads straight down for 70 pips do to previous CP.

این اولین تلاشمه برای تحلیل تکنیکال S&D. همچنین اولین باریه که هر نوع تحلیل تکنیکال درباره‌ی FX رو می‌نویسم.

تمرین فشردگی بخش 1 تایم‌فریم پایین‌تر 15M

1. همون‌طور که PA بین زون‌های عرضه و تقاضا حرکت می‌کنه توی این مورد فشردگی زیادی هست

2. سفارش‌های خرید موقع بازآزمایی زون تقاضا پر میشن و یه صعود راحت 40 پیپی به‌خاطر CP قبلی اتفاق میفته

3. توی چهارمین بازآزمایی زون عرضه سفارش فروش جدی کافی پیدا نمیشه و یه فلگ صعودی درست زیر خط عرضه شکل می‌گیره، قیمت از فلگ و از زون عرضه بیرون می‌زنه و 50 پیپ دیگه میره.

4. همون‌طور که قیمت خط عرضه‌ی قبلی رو تست می‌کنه که الان حمایت شده، یه فلگ نزولی می‌سازه و به‌راحتی به‌خاطر CP قبلی 30 پیپ پایین می‌افته.

5. دوباره قیمت شروع می‌کنه به سرگردوندن بین زون‌های عرضه و تقاضا توی فشردگی بزرگ تا اینکه بتونه وارد زون تقاضا بشه، سفارش‌های کافی رو جمع کنه تا به زون عرضه‌ی حالا چندین بار تست‌شده و دو بار شکسته‌شده برسه.

6. از اینجا سوار راحتی به پایینه با مقاومت زیاد توی زون تقاضا چون اون رو می‌شکنه و مستقیم برای 70 پیپ میره به‌خاطر CP قبلی.

This is my first post on this forum.

I like to digest an idea, mull it over for a while and then express the idea verbally to see if it makes sense. This is what I am doing here. Once I am comfortable I have digested the idea, the practice may begin. In this post, I am going to verbalise my understanding of compression, but more importantly, how it is of benefit to a trader.

Trading charts is similar to playing sport. In sport, we need to use different tactics at different places on the field. Have you watched Australia Ruby League (Australia football)? If so, what do you find in the middle of the field? You will find mud, blood, injuries and so on. It is not where you look to execute your key plays.

Rather, you want to execute your key plays where they count. This is near the try (score/goal/touch down) line. You do not use your key plays anywhere on the field. You wait until your team is in position, a place where you have an opportunity to score. Then, when the conditions are right, you execute your key plays. In trading, your key plays are your entry techniques and where you use them matters.

As a trader, we need to identify areas of opportunity, a place on the chart where the odds are significantly in our favour. Strong supply and demand levels provide this opportunity. These are places on a chart where a move may start from. This is where we can bring out our key plays out and score a touch-down.

At a strong supply level, we expect there to be an overwhelming volume of sell orders and price to fall. At a strong demand level, we expect there to be an overwhelming volume of buy orders and price to rise. However, like in our sports analogy, the team may be at the right place on the field, but your key players may not yet be positioned for the best possible opportunity. However, once everyone is in place, it’s time to go for the touch-down.

Once we are in the right position on a chart, how can we tell if the odds are significantly in our favour? That is the important question. In other words, if we are at a significant demand level and ready to short, what conditions would prevent price falling rapidly?

The only thing which will stop price falling (sessions times, news, etc. aside) are buy orders waiting to be consumed, pushing price back up, or stalling the fall. However, if there were no buy orders waiting to be consumed below the current price level, the selling pressure at a supply level would cause the price to fall rapidly. Price is free to drop until it once again reaches a demand level where new buyers are waiting.

This can be summarised as follows:

- We want to short at a strong supply level if we believe the buy orders lurking below the current price were consumed in the up move.

- We want to buy at a strong demand level if we believe thee sell orders lurking above the current price were consumed in the down move.

We know when we are at a supply or demand level. We can see this on the chart. The problem is, we cannot see how many buy orders are sitting below us, nor can we see how many sell orders are sitting above us. However, we can make an educated guess about what orders may be lurking by visually recognising what the consumption of previous orders looks like on a chart.

The visual recognition of the consumption of orders on a chart is called compression.

If price is moving up and compressing, the buy orders are being consumed. If the buy orders have been consumed, they are not lurking below the current price. As such, when price hits a strong supply level and selling pressure kicks in, price has a clear path to drop straight back through the area of compression. Price is free to drop as there are no pockets of buy orders waiting to be consumed. Price will drop until it reaches a demand level where new buyers are waiting.

Likewise, if price is moving down and compressing, the sell orders are being

consumed. If the sell orders have been consumed, they are not lurking above the current price. As such, when price hits a strong demand level and buying pressure kicks in, price has a clear path to climb straight up through the area of compression. Price climbs as there are no longer pockets of sell orders waiting to be consumed. Price is free to climb until it reaches a supply level where new sellers are waiting.

For this reason:

- An ideal reversal point for a short position is at a strong supply level where price compressed into the supply.

- An ideal reversal point for a long position is at a strong demand level where price compressed into the demand.

By knowing this, the demand and supply zones can define where you want to bring out your key plays, and the compression tells you it’s an ideal time to place your chips on the table. This is why recognising and understanding compression is important to price action trading.

In my next post, I will describe what compression looks like on a chart and what is happening inside the compression. I hope other people find this post useful.

این اولین پستم توی این فورومه.

دوست دارم یه ایده رو هضم کنم، یه مدتی روش فکر کنم و بعد ایده رو کلامی بیان کنم ببینم منطقیه یا نه. همین کار رو اینجا دارم می‌کنم. وقتی راحت شدم که ایده رو هضم کردم، تمرین می‌تونه شروع بشه. توی این پست می‌خوام فهمم از فشردگی رو کلامی بیان کنم، ولی مهم‌تر، این‌که چطور به یه معامله‌گر سود می‌رسونه.

معامله چارت شبیه بازی ورزشه. توی ورزش باید توی نقاط مختلف زمین از تاکتیک‌های مختلف استفاده کنیم. فوتبال استرالیا (Rugby League) رو دیدی؟ اگه آره، توی وسط زمین چی پیدا می‌کنی؟ گِل، خون، مصدومیت و اینا رو پیدا می‌کنی. اونجا نیست که دنبال اجرا کردن حرکت‌های کلیدیت می‌گردی.

بلکه می‌خوای حرکت‌های کلیدیت رو جایی که به حساب میاد اجرا کنی. این نزدیک خط try (گل/امتیاز) هست. حرکت‌های کلیدیت رو توی هر جای زمین استفاده نمی‌کنی. صبر می‌کنی تیمت توی موقعیت قرار بگیره، جایی که فرصت امتیاز گرفتن داری. بعد وقتی شرایط درست شد، حرکت‌های کلیدیت رو اجرا می‌کنی. توی ترید، حرکت‌های کلیدیت تکنیک‌های ورودی‌ت هستن و مهمه کجا ازشون استفاده می‌کنی.

به‌عنوان معامله‌گر باید نواحی فرصت رو تشخیص بدیم، جایی روی چارت که شانس به‌طور قابل‌توجهی به نفع ماست. سطوح قوی عرضه و تقاضا این فرصت رو فراهم می‌کنن. اینا جاهایی روی چارتن که یه حرکت می‌تونه از اونجا شروع بشه. اینجاست که می‌تونیم حرکت‌های کلیدیمون رو بیرون بیاریم و touchdown بزنیم.

توی یه سطح عرضه‌ی قوی انتظار داریم حجم عظیمی از سفارش‌های فروش باشه و قیمت بیفته. توی یه سطح تقاضای قوی انتظار داریم حجم عظیمی از سفارش‌های خرید باشه و قیمت بالا بره. با این حال، مثل تشبیه ورزشی‌مون، تیم ممکنه جای درست زمین باشه، ولی بازیکنان کلیدی‌ت هنوز برای بهترین فرصت ممکن مستقر نشده باشن. با این حال، وقتی همه سر جاشون بودن، وقتشه برای touchdown بری.

وقتی توی موقعیت درست روی یه چارت هستیم، چطور بفهمیم شانس به‌طور قابل‌توجهی به نفع ماست؟ این سؤال مهمه. به عبارت دیگه، اگه توی یه سطح تقاضای مهم هستیم و آماده‌ی شورتیم، چه شرایطی جلوی سقوط سریع قیمت رو می‌گیره؟

تنها چیزی که جلوی سقوط قیمت رو می‌گیره (به‌جز زمان‌های سشن، اخبار و غیره) سفارش‌های خریده که منتظر مصرف شدنن، قیمت رو برمی‌گردونن بالا، یا ریزش رو متوقف می‌کنن. با این حال، اگه هیچ سفارش خریدی زیر سطح قیمت فعلی منتظر مصرف نباشه، فشار فروش روی یه سطح عرضه باعث میشه قیمت به‌سرعت بیفته. قیمت آزاده بیفته تا وقتی دوباره به یه سطح تقاضا برسه که خریداران جدید منتظرن.

این رو می‌شه این‌طوری خلاصه کرد:

می‌خوایم روی یه سطح عرضه‌ی قوی فروش کنیم اگه باور داریم سفارش‌های خریدی که زیر قیمت فعلی کمین کردن توی حرکت صعودی مصرف شدن.

می‌خوایم روی یه سطح تقاضای قوی بای کنیم اگه باور داریم سفارش‌های فروشی که بالای قیمت فعلی کمین کردن توی حرکت نزولی مصرف شدن.

می‌دونیم کی روی سطح عرضه یا تقاضا هستیم. این رو می‌شه روی چارت دید. مشکل اینه که نمی‌تونیم ببینیم چند تا سفارش خرید زیرمون نشسته و نه می‌تونیم ببینیم چند تا سفارش فروش بالایمون نشسته. با این حال، می‌تونیم با تشخیص بصری این‌که مصرف سفارش‌های قبلی روی چارت چه شکلیه، حدس هوشمندانه‌ای درباره‌ی این‌که چه سفارش‌هایی ممکنه کمین کرده باشن بزنیم.

تشخیص بصری مصرف سفارش‌ها روی چارت فشردگی نامیده میشه.

اگه قیمت داره بالا میره و فشرده میشه، سفارش‌های خرید دارن مصرف میشن. اگه سفارش‌های خرید مصرف شده باشن، دیگه زیر قیمت فعلی کمین نکردن. پس وقتی قیمت به یه سطح عرضه‌ی قوی می‌رسه و فشار فروش فعال میشه، قیمت راه صاف داره که مستقیم از ناحیه‌ی فشردگی برگرده پایین. قیمت آزاده بیفته چون جیب سفارش‌های خریدی نیست که منتظر مصرف باشن. قیمت می‌افته تا وقتی به یه سطح تقاضا برسه که خریداران جدید منتظرن.

همین‌طور، اگه قیمت داره پایین میره و فشرده میشه، سفارش‌های فروش دارن

مصرف میشن. اگه سفارش‌های فروش مصرف شده باشن، دیگه بالای قیمت فعلی کمین نکردن. پس وقتی قیمت به یه سطح تقاضای قوی می‌رسه و فشار خرید فعال میشه، قیمت راه صاف داره که مستقیم از ناحیه‌ی فشردگی بالا بره. قیمت بالا میره چون دیگه جیب سفارش‌های فروشی نیست که منتظر مصرف باشن. قیمت آزاده بالا بره تا وقتی به یه سطح عرضه برسه که فروشندگان جدید منتظرن.

به همین دلیل:

نقطه‌ی برگشت ایده‌آل برای پوزیشن فروش روی یه سطح عرضه‌ی قویه که قیمت به‌سمتش فشرده شده باشه.

نقطه‌ی برگشت ایده‌آل برای پوزیشن خرید روی یه سطح تقاضای قویه که قیمت به‌سمتش فشرده شده باشه.

با دونستن این، زون‌های تقاضا و عرضه می‌تونن تعیین کنن کجا می‌خوای حرکت‌های کلیدیت رو بیرون بیاری، و فشردگی بهت میگه زمان ایده‌آلیه که ژتونهات رو روی میز بذاری. برای همین تشخیص و فهمیدن فشردگی برای معامله پرایس اکشن مهمه.

توی پست بعدیم توضیح میدم فشردگی روی چارت چه شکلیه و داخل فشردگی چه اتفاقی میفته. امیدوارم بقیه این پست رو مفید بدونن.

In my last post, I described what compression is and why it is important. However, I did not describe what compression looks like on screen. In this post, I will describe what compression looks like on screen so that compression may be more easily recognised.

Price will rise when there are more buy orders than sell orders. We can see this visually. Price is rising and making higher highs and higher lows. Therefore we know that the buyers are in charge and driving price higher. In the same way, price will fall when there are more sell orders than buy orders. We can see this visually. Price is falling and making lower lows and lower highs. Therefore, we know the sellers are in charge pushing price lower.

If prices are rising and the buyers are in charge that is good. We need the buyers to push prices up to a major supply level where we are patiently waiting to sell. However, when we are ready to sell, we want the buyers which have moved price up to our major supply level to be exhausted. We do not want to get into a fight with the buyers. If they are exhausted, the will put up a small fight, and then crumble under the selling pressure. In order words, we want their buys orders to have been all consumed. We do not want buyers to still be vigorously chasing price up.

What is important is the way price is moving on screen, not just the fact price is moving up or moving down. If price is moving up, buyers will be keen to join the up-trend, or add new longs to their existing bullish position. However, buyers will generally prefer to buy at a price which they perceive to be good value. In order to buy at a price of good value, buyers wait for a pull-back to get in at a better price. However, they dare not wait for too much of a pull-back or they may miss the boat. Buy orders will usually be placed and sit eagerly awaiting price to come back to the most recent minor demand level. This is the last place from which price moved up or the most recent minor swing low.

If this is the case, price dips into the most recent minor demand and the buy orders are consumed. The consumption of these orders shoots the price back up. How this looks on screen depends on the time frame, though will often appear as candles with long lower wicks. How far price moves up depends on the how many excited buyers there are. If there are a significant number of buyers, price will zoom! However, this is not the price action that forms compression. In compression, there will be enough buyers to push prices up, possibly creating long lower wicks, but once the buy orders at perceived good value are consumed, price will move up steadily again.

As the trend continues, the process repeats over. Price dips, buyers step in at the most recent minor demand and price makes a new higher low.

- When price is rising, but with dips which spike down, you are seeing compression in the up move. When you see this, you know that the buys orders are being consumed on the pull-backs in the up move.

- When price is falling but with spikes up, you are seeing compression in the down move. When you see this, you know that the sell orders are being consumed on the rallies in the down move.

توی پست آخرم توضیح دادم فشردگی چیه و چرا مهمه. با این حال، توضیح ندادم فشردگی روی صفحه چه شکلیه. توی این پست توضیح میدم فشردگی روی صفحه چه شکلیه تا فشردگی راحت‌تر تشخیص داده بشه.

قیمت وقتی بالا میره که سفارش‌های خرید از سفارش‌های فروش بیشتر باشن. این رو می‌شه بصری دید. قیمت داره بالا میره و سقف‌ها و کف‌های بالاتر می‌سازه. پس می‌دونیم خریدارها کنترل رو دست دارن و قیمت رو بالاتر می‌برن. به همین ترتیب، قیمت وقتی می‌افته که سفارش‌های فروش از سفارش‌های خرید بیشتر باشن. این رو می‌شه بصری دید. قیمت داره می‌افته و کف‌ها و سقف‌های پایین‌تر می‌سازه. پس می‌دونیم فروشندگان کنترل رو دست دارن و قیمت رو پایین‌تر می‌برن.

اگه قیمتها دارن بالا میرن و خریدارها کنترل رو دست دارن خوبه. باید خریدارها قیمتها رو تا یه سطح عرضه‌ی مهم ببرن بالا که ما صبورانه منتظر فروش اونجاییم. با این حال، وقتی آماده‌ی فروش شدیم، می‌خوایم خریدارهایی که قیمت رو تا سطح عرضه‌ی بزرگمون بردن بالا خسته شده باشن. نمی‌خوایم وارد جنگ با خریدارها بشیم. اگه خسته شده باشن، یه درگیری کوچیک می‌کنن و بعد زیر فشار فروش خرد میشن. به عبارت دیگه، می‌خوایم همه‌ی سفارش‌های خریدشون مصرف شده باشه. نمی‌خوایم خریدارها هنوز با اشتیاق قیمت رو به بالا تعقیب کنن.

مهم اینه که قیمت روی صفحه چطور داره حرکت می‌کنه، نه فقط این‌که قیمت بالا میره یا پایین. اگه قیمت داره بالا میره، خریدارها مشتاق میشن به روند صعودی ملحق بشن یا خرید‌های جدید به پوزیشن صعودی موجودشون اضافه کنن. با این حال، خریدارها معمولاً ترجیح میدن قیمت رو بخرن که اون رو ارزش خوب می‌دونن. برای خرید قیمت با ارزش خوب، خریدارها منتظر پولبک می‌مونن تا با قیمت بهتر وارد بشن. با این حال، جرأت نمی‌کنن منتظر pull-back زیادی بمونن وگرنه ممکنه قافله رو از دست بدن. سفارش‌های خرید معمولاً گذاشته میشن و با اشتیاق منتظر می‌مونن قیمت برگرده به آخرین سطح تقاضای جزئی. این آخرین جاییه که قیمت از اونجا بالا رفته یا آخرین swing low جزئی.

اگه اینطور باشه، قیمت به آخرین تقاضای جزئی فرو می‌ره و سفارش‌های خرید مصرف میشن. مصرف این سفارش‌ها قیمت رو به بالا شلیک می‌کنه. این روی صفحه چه شکلیه بستگی به تایم‌فریم داره، ولی اغلب به‌صورت کندل‌هایی با فیتیله‌های پایینی بلند ظاهر میشه. قیمت چقدر بالا میره بستگی داره به اینکه چند تا خریدار هیجان‌زده هستن. اگه تعداد قابل‌توجهی خریدار باشه، قیمت می‌پره! با این حال، این همون پرایس‌اکشنی نیست که فشردگی رو می‌سازه. توی فشردگی، به‌اندازه‌ی کافی خریدار هست که قیمت‌ها رو ببره بالا، شاید فیتیله‌های پایینی بلند بسازه، ولی وقتی سفارش‌های خرید روی ارزش خوبِ درک‌شده مصرف شدن، قیمت دوباره به‌طور ثابت بالا میره.

همون‌طور که روند ادامه پیدا می‌کنه، این پروسه تکرار میشه. قیمت فرو می‌ره، خریدارها توی آخرین تقاضای جزئی وارد میشن و قیمت کف بالاتری می‌سازه.

وقتی قیمت داره بالا میره ولی با فرو رفتن‌هایی که به پایین پیک می‌زنن، داری فشردگی توی حرکت صعودی رو می‌بینی. وقتی این رو می‌بینی، می‌دونی سفارش‌های خرید روی pull-بازگشتای حرکت صعودی دارن مصرف میشن.

وقتی قیمت داره می‌افته ولی با پیک‌های بالا، داری فشردگی توی حرکت نزولی رو می‌بینی. وقتی این رو می‌بینی، می‌دونی سفارش‌های فروش روی رالی‌های حرکت نزولی دارن مصرف میشن.

یه مثال از فشردگی پایین نشون داده شده. توی پست بعدیم چند راهی رو نشون میدم که فشردگی می‌تونه روی صفحه ظاهر بشه. امیدوارم بقیه این پست رو مفید بدونن.

And if this seems tedious to you in anyway, do not worry about that. Keep telling yourself this story as you look into the charts and even when you post charts. I am looking at the break down of price on the Euro as per the chart below. I was expecting the break down for other reasons, but from a price action perspective, the question to ask is why did price choose that level from which to break down? Why not 20 pips below that level or 20 pips above that level? Is there a reason for that exact level?

It's all about decisions on price. The question the market is asking is this. Is price too cheap or is too expensive?

Decisions are made all the time. However, important decisions are remembered. If the market decided that $1 is way too cheap, there is a mad rush to buy driving price up. That is strong demand. When price comes back to $1 the market remembers this and it is time to buy again, assuming market conditions have not changed.

I refer to the market, but what is that? Most people consider the market as the collective of traders. I would challenge that thought as the collective of traders is the crowd. When the market makes an important decision, it is not the crowd that decides. The crowd would most likely get it wrong. Let’s assume the market is getting it right. As such, important decisions on price, the decisions that count, are not made by the crowd. These decisions are made by the smart money and their decisions determine where price goes at important price levels.

The collective of smart money are still people and it pays to understand how people make decisions. It is often said that successful people make firm decisions. That is, important decisions once made are carried out with enthusiasm and energy. The question is, can we see this decision making process play out visually on our charts?

When decisions are made, especially if there is significant money on the line, people will pause and consider their options. Traders will look at lines, levels and indicators. They may check the fundamentals. They may check for signs of confirmation in many ways. They pause and ponder if the decision they are about to make is the right one. We see this when price stalls.

Goods examples are the rally-base-rally, drop-base-drop, rally-base-drop and drop-base-rally price patterns. In these examples, the decision is happening in the base. Is price now too expensive or is it still too cheap? If it is an important decision, once it is decided, the orders pile on. We see the result of that decision when we observe a pole.

The market is going up and down all the time. So in effect, decisions are being made all the time, tick by tick, candle by candle. What we are concerned with is recognising when a significantly important decision has been made and what that decision looks like on screen. If the market decides that $1 is way too cheap, then it pays to listen to that decision. If Warren Buffett whispered in my ear that company X shares were cheap at $1, it would pay to listen to that. When price pulled back to $1 dollar, it would be time to buy, and buy aggressively.

Let’s assume for the moment that the exact price from where the Euro collapsed was at a prior decision on price. It was not at some random price point. That is, it was decided earlier that the Euro at price was too expensive and that was an important decision. When price comes back to that price, this is something we would want to know about it. Before the Euro collapsed, we had a rally and then a base. When the price stalled, the market had to make a decision. Is price still too expensive?

The market decided that the Euro was still too expensive and price collapsed. In my next post, I will go back and see what that prior decision looks like.

I am looking at the price where Euro collapsed and asking myself why the market decided that price was too expensive. More importantly, I am interested in observing what that decision looks like on screen. I can see that the Euro fell from there, but the market does not pay for noticing things in hindsight. The market pays when we correctly anticipate what may happen in the future and we are rewarded for our ability to act on that in a well risk defined manner. However, in order to do this, we need to know at what places we should to be paying attention, perched ready to pounce.

Prior to the collapse there was a rally and a base (see post #8 above). In the base the market was making a decision. The market was deciding if price was too cheap or too expensive. If the market decides price is too cheap, we will see a rally-base-rally develop. If the market decides price is too expensive, we will see rally-base-drop. It turns out we had a rally-base-drop, but that was only seen after that fact.

The weekly chart shows important decisions were made around this price level in the past.

The daily chart is more insightful, showing with more clarity the decisions being made around this price.

The 4hr chart shows the level being crossed up and down numerous times.

The 1hr chart shows some historical significance at this price level. The last time was around the 10th of October. I will take a closer look and see what happened at this time.

The 5min chart shows the market making decisions. The market decides price was too cheap on the 11th of October. The challenge I have is that I can see these decisions playing out at all different price levels on the chart. As mentioned, this is all in hindsight and I cannot trade in hindsight.

To me, the most useful piece of information on the chart, and what I would most likely be looking at in real time is the most recent demand marked in the green box. I say this as it just sticks out so clearly. When price reached this level, the market considered the Euro as cheap and there was strong demand for the Euro at this price. On the last test of the level, the demand was very strong and price zoomed away. The demand created a traditional support level.

What catches my eye was is fact that price moved away abruptly on testing the level. That is, the market did not wallow around at this price making a decision on the value of the Euro. The smart money had decided well before the Euro reached this price that it was cheap and the buy orders were eagerly waiting price to reach that level.

The question is, when prices comes back to that level again, what will happen? Will there still be demand at that price. If so, how much? If there is demand, the price will move up once again. However, there is only a finite amount of demand for a commodity at certain price. Once all the buyers have made their purchase, the demand disappears. The market is big, but it is still finite. Once the buyers have had their fill, the demand will have been all consumed.

When the Euro comes back to the level, price bases. That is, it forms a drop-base structure. Price did not zoom away. It’s during that base the a decision is being made. Is price still cheap? Or, is it now too expensive? It's time to decide? This is what the decision making process looks like zoomed out.

And this is what it looks like zoomed in.

The market decides price is too expensive. All the demand is consumed. Price falls away, leaving fresh supply. In the decision making process, what I see on screen is a S/R flip.

When price comes back to a S/R flip zone, a place where market changed its mind on the value of the Euro, that is the price at which the Euro collapsed. It's somewhere I should be looking at. In this case, it was a place where there was prior demand. But once that demand was consumed, what was left was fresh supply.

وقتی یورو به اون سطح برمی‌گرده، قیمت base میگیره. یعنی، ساختار drop-base رو می‌سازه. قیمت با شتاب نرفت. تصمیم داخل اون base داره گرفته میشه. آیا قیمت هنوز ارزونه؟ یا الان خیلی گرونه؟ وقتشه تصمیم بگیره؟ این چیزیه که پروسه‌ی تصمیم‌گیری موقع نمای دور این‌شکلیه.

و این چیزیه که موقع نمای نزدیک این‌شکلیه.

بازار تصمیم می‌گیره قیمت خیلی گرونه. همه‌ی تقاضا مصرف میشه. قیمت می‌ره و عرضه‌ی تازه به جا می‌ذاره. توی پروسه‌ی تصمیم‌گیری، چیزی که روی صفحه می‌بینم یه S/R flip هست.

وقتی قیمت به یه زون S/R flip برمی‌گرده، جایی که بازار نظرش رو روی ارزش یورو عوض کرده، اون قیمتیه که یورو اونجا فروپاشید. جاییه که باید بهش نگاه کنم. توی این مورد، جایی بود که تقاضای قبلی اونجا بود. ولی وقتی اون تقاضا مصرف شد، چیزی که موند عرضه‌ی تازه بود.

خوشحالم که هنوز فعاله:) حدس می‌زنم یه کم دیر رسیدم، ولی این اولین تلاشم برای تشخیص CP‌ه. هر روشی که بتونم بهتر بشم بگید:

ویدئوهای IF رو دیده بودم و همیشه یه توضیحی داشت که چرا قیمت توی یه نقطه‌ی خاص نوسان می‌کنه. اون پیک توی کندل رو متوجه شدم و فقط کنجکاو بودم چرا این اتفاق میفته. یه باکس زرد از اون نقطه به چپ گذاشتم ولی نتونستم چیزی پیدا کنم که باعث این بشه.

Yes, there's a very good reason for that PA

Firstly, there were a mass of buy orders remaining at the bottom of your yellow box -supply breaking like that will nearly always leave unfilled buys These needed to be consumed before price could drop

Then we come to the break above the spike high. If you want to sell lots and lots of something, you need lots and lots of buyers So what do you do to get lots and lots of buyers? You Breakout above an high. This will fill lots of stop losses from the more idiotic retail traders (always remember that a sl on a sell is a buy), and also excite new idiots into buying.

So then what have you got? You have the buy orders beneath you all used up, and you have tons of buy orders to sell to, so you get your bucketload of shorts in with nothing to stop price from falling hard back into the pole

Very simple stuff

خب پس بگذارید شروع کنم: فشرده‌سازی برای پر کردن سفارش‌های پرنشده بعد از وقوع LQ استفاده می‌شود. وقتی فروشنده‌ها بیشتر از خریدارها باشند و عرضه همیشه با فشرده‌سازی رعایت شود، ریزش همچنان معتبر است. وقتی LQ از سمت فروشنده‌ها نمی‌تواند ریزش را جلو ببرد، این می‌تواند به تقاضا تبدیل شود. ببین خریدارها وقتی LQ فروشنده‌ها شکست می‌خورد چه واکنشی نشان می‌دهند؛ اگر در پاسخ LQ گاوی باشد که آن عرضه را ENG کند، ممکن است تغییری رخ دهد. اگر واکنش برگشتی هم یک CP نسبتاً ضعیف باشد و باز هم عرضه رعایت شود، چیزی عوض نشده، فقط یک خستگی جزئی فروشنده‌ها است، ولی نشانهٔ ضعف در سمت گاوی. درست است؟

برعکسش هم وقتی خریدارها بیشتر از فروشنده‌ها باشند، که در مثال نشان داده شده.

یک ریفیل می‌تواند به‌صورت FO به سمت منبع رخ دهد، یا به‌صورت یک FTR. هر دو نشانه‌های قوی هستند و ویژگی دیگری به ساختار و به اینکه قیمت بعدش کجا می‌خواهد برود اضافه می‌کنند.

پس برای من این‌طور است:

CP بعد از LQ با توجه به ناحیه. یا CP بعد از CP، نشانهٔ خستگی (نه بیشتر)، یا CP و بعد از آن LQ در راستای همان CP (ریزشی از یک رالی به‌خاطر بی‌علاقگی طرف مقابل)

I'd also love to get IF's opinion on the engulf you pointed out and whether or not that candle (or the one before?) would have been a sensible time to enter based on his engulf the demand suggestion for trading CP.

This is how I see it all unfolding (from left to right following price and numbers on chart):

1) At this level we see only a small amount of candles in the base and also a large jump away of price. So we had way too many buy orders - price could not stay here for very long and moved away very fast. A sign that pro money has a stack of buy orders here.

2) Price moved up and pro money started taking profits - this shown by the candles with lots of wicks. Since they have open buy orders they need to counter trade with sell orders to exit their positions, this obviously sending the market back down from the highs.

3) All of this profit taking eventually sends price back down. Shown by big red candle.

4) That is the start of the compression. Big money knows they still have a stack of buy orders they need filled (at point 1) so they try and push price down to that level so they can get filled at the best possible price. At the same time they try and remove all resistance to price so that once it reaches 1 it can shoot back up without any supply to slow it down. So begins the slow process of taking out all the decision points on the way down.

5) Because of recent down trend caused by compression, many retail traders will try and follow the trend - "the trend is your friend" mentality. So they sell the continuation of the trend (sell orders placed at lower black line and stops at upper black line). These sell orders helps fill pro money buy orders - when retail sells pro takes their buys. Price also touched their stack of buy orders (from 1) and shot back up.

6) Their massive amount of buy orders at 1 pushed price higher. Once it broke the recent highs everyone who was short at 5 freaked out and exited their position (or got stopped out) creating even more buy orders which pushes price even higher.

7) Once price got back up to acceptable level pro money started taking profits again which sent price back down.

I'm not sure if this is right. Please try and pull this apart. I'd rather be wrong and learn something than people agreeing with me.

این‌طور می‌بینم که ماجرا شکل می‌گیرد (از چپ به راست، دنبال کردن قیمت و اعداد روی چارت):

1) در این سطح فقط تعداد کمی کندل در بیس می‌بینیم و همچنین یک جهش بزرگ قیمت. یعنی سفارش خرید خیلی زیاد داشتیم — قیمت نمی‌توانست مدت زیادی اینجا بماند و خیلی سریع دور شد. نشانه‌ای از اینکه پول حرفه‌ای اینجا انبوهی سفارش خرید دارد.

2) قیمت بالا رفت و پول حرفه‌ای شروع کرد به سود گرفتن — این را از کندل‌های پرسایه می‌بینیم. چون سفارش‌های خریدشان باز است، باید با سفارش فروش معاملهٔ معکوس بزنند تا از پوزیشن خارج شوند؛ طبیعتاً همین بازار را از سقف‌ها به پایین برمی‌گرداند.

3) همهٔ این سود گرفتن‌ها در نهایت قیمت را به پایین برمی‌گرداند. با کندل قرمز بزرگ مشخص است.

4) اینجاست که فشرده‌سازی شروع می‌شود. پول بزرگ می‌داند هنوز انبوهی سفارش خرید دارد که باید پر شود (در نقطهٔ 1)، پس سعی می‌کند قیمت را تا آن سطح پایین ببرد تا با بهترین قیمت ممکن پر شود. همزمان می‌کوشد همهٔ مقاومت‌ها را از سر راه قیمت بردارد تا وقتی به 1 رسید، بدون عرضه‌ای که کندش کند، دوباره شلیک کند. این‌طور روند آرام پاک کردن همهٔ نقاط تصمیم در مسیر نزول شروع می‌شود.

5) به خاطر روند نزولی اخیری که فشرده‌سازی ایجاد کرده، خیلی از معامله‌گران خرد سعی می‌کنند روند را دنبال کنند — طرز فکر «روند دوست توست». پس ادامهٔ روند را می‌فروشند (سفارش‌های فروش روی خط مشکی پایین و استاپ‌ها روی خط مشکی بالا). این سفارش‌های فروش به پر شدن سفارش‌های خرید پول حرفه‌ای کمک می‌کند — وقتی خرد می‌فروشد، پول حرفه‌ای خریدش را برمی‌دارد. قیمت هم به انبوه سفارش‌های خریدش (از 1) خورد و برگشت بالا.

6) حجم عظیم سفارش‌های خریدشان در 1 قیمت را بالاتر برد. وقتی سقف‌های اخیر شکست، هر کسی که در 5 فروش بود ترسید و از پوزیشنش خارج شد (یا استاپ خورد) و سفارش خرید بیشتری ساخت که قیمت را باز هم بالاتر می‌برد.

7) وقتی قیمت برگشت به سطح قابل قبول، پول حرفه‌ای دوباره شروع به سود گرفتن کرد و قیمت به پایین برگشت.

مطمئن نیستم این درست باشد. لطفاً نقدش کن و تکه‌تکه‌اش کن. ترجیح می‌دهم اشتباه باشم و چیزی یاد بگیرم تا اینکه مردم با من موافق باشند.

خب این چارت واقعاً شلوغ است، PA اصلاً نرم نیست، اما باید بتوانیم در همهٔ شرایط تحلیل کنیم و معامله کنیم…

هر بار که شروع به نگاه کردن به چارت‌ها می‌کنم، سعی می‌کنم این سؤال را بپرسم: «تصمیم کجا گرفته شد؟» و با این چارت جواب دادن به آن سؤال خیلی سخت است، هرچند غیرممکن نه.

نظرات دربارهٔ چارت پیوست: 1. RBD تشکیل شد (دکل نزولی بزرگ) ~ تصمیم بر این بود که قیمت بیش از حد گران است 2. یک FL هست، بعد از آن یک FL دیگر، یک DBR (هرچند این مشکوک است، چون قیمت رالی نکرد و بیشتر نوعی CP یا بلاتصمیمی است) 3. رالی، با یک FL ~ DP، و همان‌طور که قیمت بالا رفت، مطمئنم در دکل نزولی سمت چپ یک DP هست که آن واکنش را ایجاد کرد. 4. نقطه‌های 4 و 5 جایی است که واقعاً شلوغ می‌شود (خودم می‌دانم که این به‌خاطر خبر NFP بود) 5. RBD، باز هم واقعاً افت نیست، بیشتر CP، با یک اسپایک به بالا برای تست یک DP در 5. 6. افت، بیس و بعد فشردگی با یک رالی یا کندل نقدینگی به داخل ناحیهٔ عرضه 7. RBD تشکیل شد 8. DB و بعد از آن CP 9. CP رو به بالا، با مصرف عرضه، همراه با چند DP 10. قیمت تا 1 رالی کرد، DP قبلی را تست کرد و یک RBD ~ DP ~ ناحیهٔ عرضهٔ جدید ساخت 11. CP رو به پایین، با مصرف تقاضا 12. CP، اما این یکی بیشتر افت است (رالی نزولی) 13. DBD، که یک FL هم هست 14. DB، و بعد از آن CP… یا احتمالاً یک بیس بزرگ 15. CP بیشتر، تست بیس در 14. 16. DBR ~ تصمیم بر این بود که قیمت بیش از حد ارزان است

Ifmyante wrote: Compression is one of the most important signs that price is getting ready to turn.

As price is rising into Supply, it keeps dropping as it goes, filling the buy orders left at each Demand on the way up, allowing a quick drop through the CP zone when price hits Supply.

The exact opposite is true for Compression into Demand.

Here it is explained in a video

Homework

Set up a subfolder for CP Homework and get into the charts

Find at least 20 CP setups, at HTF S/D zones, and explain what you see on each chart

Also chart the bigger picture where the CP occurred

While you're looking for CP, take the time to find at least 20 CPLQ (Liquidity) too

If you're not used to these, you can get stopped out of some fantastic trades and deeply regret not knowing why.

Ifmyante نوشت: فشردگی یکی از مهم‌ترین نشانه‌های آماده شدن قیمت برای برگشته.

همون‌طور که قیمت به سمت عرضه بالا می‌ره، در مسیر مدام پایین می‌آد و سفارش‌های خریدی که در هر تقاضا در راه بالا جا مونده رو پر می‌کنه، و همین اجازه می‌ده وقتی قیمت به عرضه می‌رسه یک ریزش سریع از ناحیهٔ CP داشته باشه.

دقیقاً برعکسش برای فشردگی به سمت تقاضا صادقه.

اینجا در یک ویدئو توضیح داده شده

تکلیف

یک زیرپوشه برای تکلیف CP بساز و برو سراغ چارت‌ها

حداقل 20 ستاپ CP، در ناحیه‌های S/D تایم‌فریم بالاتر پیدا کن و برای هر چارت توضیح بده چی می‌بینی

همچنین تصویر بزرگ‌تری که CP در آن رخ داده رو چارت کن

وقتی دنبال CP می‌گردی، وقت بذار و حداقل 20 تا CPLQ (نقدینگی) هم پیدا کن

اگه به این‌ها عادت نداری، ممکنه از چند معاملهٔ فوق‌العاده استاپ بخوری و عمیقاً حسرت بخوری که چرا دلیلش رو نمی‌دونستی.

It is not in my plan at all to be trading demo or even test trading yet, but I could not resist and wanted to see how I dealt with it.

I hope I can explain this as I saw it, here goes....

I saw on the weekly we were in a Demand buying zone, so I was watching all the other lower time frames for potential P.A set ups.

I finally found quite good P.A on the hourly, first off I saw average CP, the white zones are what I believed to be consumed orders, except he zone in yellow, this was still fresh. Being eager to enter a trade, I decided @ number 1 this was good enough as price seemed to consume most of the sell orders in the yellow zone, and I saw a FL @ number 2 below, so I placed a limit order to enter long and got stopped. I then saw price form a demand base @ number 3 and then the all important engulf happened @ number 4, my entry missed by two pips near number 4. So, price rallied right to my target, the end of the CP zone, and formed a nice-looking cap @ number 5. I thought considering price did not even enter my original demand zone @ 4, I believed there may have been still some buy orders left, so I left my order in place, price triggered me in @ A, and rallied to my target @ B.

A great learning experience for me, and really enjoyed it. I knew it meant nothing and no money was involved, but the nerves got tested and my emotions were still on high.

Cheers

You are correct that the candle tails shown are consuming demand at that level, though there is still some unconsumed demand (albeit, not great demand) below those candle tails. Good CP, the ones you are looking to exploit leave no (or very little) unconsumed demand on the move up.

I am at work so no access to charts. But just a few quick comments, then later I will post some charts after studying this more.

I have always only considered the top that is getting faked out, and what supply level is getting hit as the old top is getting FO'd. Of course it has to work on the buyers as well. In this situation it seems that as the? FTR got approached there has already been a long drop and sellers are probably becoming exhausted, so they can't be expected to break this demand. So the ITs have to manufacture some more sellers. It looks like maybe a 4h s/r got broken which would prompt retail sellers to adjust their stops lower above the last high. After seeing price bounce off of support and waiting for confirmation retail buys stepped in, then the emotional buyers pushed above the old top for a FO. This prompts the buyers to move up their stops, and the trap has now been laid. The ITs sell hard down to the retail sell stops. The ITs have the sells to break demand without having to do it themselves.

Now this alone raises a few questions in which the answers will be different everytime. Why would the ITs want to break that FTR in the first place? What was that FTR a failure to return to? Was it real demand, HTF support, or HTF R turned S that created the bounce that gave retail buyers confirmation? What kind of supply are we coming from? I believe the answer is in the HTFs, but this concept is brand new to me so now I must study! Thank you!

edit: one more question I thought of: Why would they not want to sell there themselves? Will be interesting to see which way the current flag resolves.

Hi Miserly_One, the idea with CP is that price retraces to remove supply or demand pockets left behind as it progresses. This allows price to easily slide back to the origin of the CP. In the cable chart today, look how price kept coming back to remove the supply pockets left behind as price dropped. This allowed price to then shoot up to the origin of the CP.

Hello revivalfx, it looks like you're fairly new here so welcome to RTM.

I think what's meant by CPLQ is: compression that leads to heavy liquidity of one type. For instance, price compresses up to a supply zone where sell orders far exceed buy orders - compression leading to sell-side liquidity.

As for your #1 and #2, I think both are correct. Sure, compression eats liquidity from both sides, but in the tight range both buys and sells are fairly evenly matched, and in the above example, price cannot make a parabolic move downward until sells absolutely overtake buys. Compression gets price to that absolute, even if that means the compression enters the zone we've drawn or moves through the zone to a higher supply zone with more sells waiting.

As for the formation, I wouldn't presume to speak for anyone on this site, but it seems like the most experienced among us pay less attention to the look of an individual candle(s) and more to the zones they create, and more specifically the orders behind the zones they create. Does a pinbar matter because of its shape after-the-fact or because demand exceed supply to drive price up where it found supply and dropped back near where price opened that bar's timeframe? In other words, the orders that created the zone that ultimately translated into a pinbar is what's important, not the bar's look/name afterwards. Where the zone occurs is also hugely important, as is who is creating the zone to begin with. These ideas have been (and continue to be) huge learning points for me - what is the smart money trying to hide from everyone else in this zone on the chart? In compression they are removing orders to make it easier to move price through that area of the chart in the future.

As you said in your P.S., if my comments above don't help you process things, it could very well be that I need to study it more. I think a lot of this has been said better elsewhere including these thoughts and charts from some of the experts: readthemarket.com/index.php/forum/journa...-on-course?start=143

سلام revivalfx، به نظر می‌رسه تازه‌واردی، پس به RTM خوش اومدی.

فکر کنم منظور از CPLQ اینه: فشردگی‌ای که به نقدینگی سنگین از یه نوع می‌رسه. مثلاً قیمت به یه زون عرضه فشرده می‌شه که توش سفارش‌های فروش خیلی بیشتر از سفارش‌های خریده — فشردگی‌ای که به نقدینگی سمت فروش می‌رسه.

دربارهٔ 1 و 2 تو، فکر کنم هر دو درستن. آره، فشردگی نقدینگی هر دو طرف رو می‌خوره، ولی توی رنج تنگ خریدها و فروش‌ها تقریباً مساوی‌ان، و توی مثال بالا قیمت نمی‌تونه حرکت سهموی به پایین بزنه تا وقتی فروش‌ها کاملاً بر خریدها غلبه کنن. فشردگی قیمت رو به همون نقطهٔ غلبه می‌رسونه، حتی اگه یعنی فشردگی وارد زونی بشه که کشیدیم یا از زون رد بشه به یه زون عرضهٔ بالاتر با فروش‌های بیشتری که منتظرن.

دربارهٔ شکل‌گیری، نمی‌خوام از طرف کسی توی این سایت حرف بزنم، ولی به نظر می‌رسه باتجربه‌ترین‌های ما کمتر به ظاهر یه کندل(ها) توجه می‌کنن و بیشتر به زون‌هایی که می‌سازن، و مشخص‌تر به سفارش‌های پشت زون‌هایی که می‌سازن. آیا پین‌بار به خاطر شکلش بعد از اتفاق مهمه یا چون تقاضا از عرضه پیشی گرفت تا قیمت رو ببره بالا، جایی که عرضه رو پیدا کرد و تا نزدیک نقطهٔ باز شدن اون کندلِ اون تایم‌فریم برگشت؟ به عبارت دیگه، سفارش‌هایی که زون رو ساختن و آخرش به یه پین‌بار تبدیل شد مهم‌ان، نه ظاهر یا اسم کندل بعدش. اینکه زون کجا شکل می‌گیره هم فوق‌العاده مهمه، و اینکه از اول چه کسی داره زون رو می‌سازه هم همینطور. این ایده‌ها برای من نقطه‌های یادگیری بزرگی بودن (و هنوز هم هستن) — پول هوشمند داره چی رو توی این زون روی چارت از بقیه پنهان می‌کنه؟ توی فشردگی اونا دارن سفارش‌ها رو برمی‌دارن تا بعداً عبور قیمت از اون قسمت چارت راحت‌تر بشه.

همون‌طور که توی پینوشت گفتی، اگه توضیحات بالام به هضم ماجرا کمکت نکرد، خیلی هم بعیده که من خودم باید بیشتر روش بخونم. فکر کنم خیلی از این حرف‌ها جای بهتری گفته شده، از جمله این افکار و چارت‌ها از بعضی از استادها: readthemarket.com/index.php/forum/journa...-on-course?start=143

دربارهٔ شکل‌گیری، نمی‌خوام از طرف کسی توی این سایت حرف بزنم، ولی به نظر می‌رسه باتجربه‌ترین‌های ما کمتر به ظاهر یه کندل(ها) توجه می‌کنن و بیشتر به زون‌هایی که می‌سازن، و مشخص‌تر به سفارش‌های پشت زون‌هایی که می‌سازن. آیا پین‌بار به خاطر شکلش بعد از اتفاق مهمه یا چون تقاضا از عرضه پیشی گرفت تا قیمت رو ببره بالا، جایی که عرضه رو پیدا کرد و تا نزدیک نقطهٔ باز شدن اون کندلِ اون تایم‌فریم برگشت؟ به عبارت دیگه، سفارش‌هایی که زون رو ساختن و آخرش به یه پین‌بار تبدیل شد مهم‌ان، نه ظاهر یا اسم کندل بعدش. اینکه زون کجا شکل می‌گیره هم فوق‌العاده مهمه، و اینکه از اول چه کسی داره زون رو می‌سازه هم همینطور. این ایده‌ها برای من نقطه‌های یادگیری بزرگی بودن (و هنوز هم هستن) — پول هوشمند داره چی رو توی این زون روی چارت از بقیه پنهان می‌کنه؟ توی فشردگی اونا دارن سفارش‌ها رو برمی‌دارن تا بعداً عبور قیمت از اون قسمت چارت راحت‌تر بشه.

Hi anneb5,

I think you might be seeing the play backwards. On my chart, you would enter at the demand I'd marked up - entering long to the top of the compression zone. On your chart, while for the most part I agree with how you've highlighted things, there are a few things I'd change from my experience. The first one is that the "H1 Supply" at the top of the compression zone may act like supply but I don't consider it to be supply myself. If you notice, it was spiked just as the other areas were in the compression zone so it should have those orders filled already. What it is, however, is often a take profit area which sometimes starts a selloff. The blue H1 Demand right below the consumed demand zones is an area I'd probably define a little more broadly. See my graphic for where I put the top/proximal line for that demand zone. Now if you were to have missed it because of being more conservative on zones, that's okay too - a friend of mine has a saying, that trades are like a bus. There's always another one coming around the corner!

Hi! The large red pole down suggest that there could be compression to the left (the wicks of the candles also gives that clue). But from this timeframe it is hard to be sure (for me:P). I would switch to 1D TF and mark all demand in this area and also mark when the demand is visited.

According to your question "New supply..." - if your compression (left) is really compression then yes, it is a great supply. Because always on the compression boundaries there are many orders. So the place where compression breaks (and FTR is made) is always an important place:) Also look how price left this level - large pole down without stopping - it also suggests that there are still many orders to be filled (which is proved when price returns to this level).

Best, Chris

LV, nice work. 2 things you need to understand regarding compression:

First thing you must know what is the meaning of compression. The compression price action show us a range of price levels where most orders packets were consumed. While this is the meaning of CP, how would you use it for you trading?

The second thing is very much the outcome of the first. Say price cp up while consuming demand below.... or the opposite, cp down while consuming supply above. these are 2 price action events we can use in the future, when price returns.

So in conclusion for your work, go back to your charts and ask yourself, do u really need to mark consumption of supply when price climbing, or can you have any use for demand consumption at price dropping....

LV، کار خوبیه. 2 چیز هست که درباره فشرده‌سازی باید بفهمی:

اولی اینه که باید بدونی معنی فشرده‌سازی چیه. پرایس اکشن فشرده‌سازی به ما یه محدوده از سطوح قیمتی نشون می‌ده که بیشتر بسته‌های سفارش در اونجا مصرف شده‌اند. این معنی CP هست، ولی چطور ازش برای معاملت استفاده می‌کنی؟

1. Compression is a signal that price will reverse its direction upon hitting a sd zone. ABSOLUTELY NOT. Compression is not a signal for anything. Compression is a price action the show us all remaining orders are been taken while progressing to a direction. Like you have a Demand or Supply zones defined, compression is a zone where NO Demand or NO Supply left.

2. Lets say price is rising to a supply zone so what happens is a compression zone is IT will push the price down price to a demand zone letting retailers to buy and then IT will again sell the price to a demand zone slowly attracting other buyers until it reached the original supply zone. So once there is no more demand left since all the retailers had filled their buy orders price will easily fall through piercing all the old demand zone. YES.

Compression tells us the is no resisting power. as you well explained, there is no demand left, and price may freely fall to the next demand below.

3. The advantage is for entry purpose we know price is going to reverse. Secondly, as our target to the base of our compression. Third, to hold the trade if we see price engulfed the compression zone we can assume that price will take another level. (this is based from what i read from other members journal, i my self have not put this into practice) Correct, as we know CP is no demand or no supply, we may be more confident to trade against it. Remember we always want to Long in a sutation of Strong Demand against weak Supply / Short in Strong Supply against weak Demand. CP show us the weak side. But never take CP as a signal - it is not a signal its oly a zone that reads a weakness for one of the two parties.

Hi Everyone My compression homework. From what I can understand Cps are a flagging area. In a bullish flag the cp will go down, consuming supply therefore making possible a move up on return. With a bearish flag you can see a CP going up while consuming demand, making it possible for the price to easily go down on return. That's why you will find poles and FLs on the left of a compressed area. Help and comments welcome!

سلام به همه، تکلیف فشردگی من. تا جایی که می‌توانم بفهمم، CP‌ها ناحیه‌ای فلگ‌مانند هستند. در یک فلگ صعودی، CP به سمت پایین می‌رود و عرضه را مصرف می‌کند و در نتیجه حرکت به سمت بالا را در بازگشت ممکن می‌کند. با یک فلگ نزولی می‌توان CP‌ای را دید که به سمت بالا می‌رود و در عین حال تقاضا را مصرف می‌کند و به قیمت اجازه می‌دهد در بازگشت به‌راحتی پایین برود. به همین دلیل است که دکل‌ها و FL‌ها را در سمت چپ یک ناحیهٔ فشرده پیدا می‌کنید. کمک و کامنت خوش‌آمد است!

Ifmyante wrote: Compression is one of the most important signs that price is getting ready to turn.

As price is rising into Supply, it keeps dropping as it goes, filling the buy orders left at each Demand on the way up, allowing a quick drop through the CP zone when price hits Supply.

The exact opposite is true for Compression into Demand.

Here is a PDF about Compression www.readthemarket.com/media/pdf/Compression.pdf

Homework

Set up a subfolder for CP Homework and get into the charts

Find at least 20 CP setups, at HTF S/D zones, and explain what you see on each chart

Also chart the bigger picture where the CP occurred

While you're looking for CP, take the time to find at least 20 CPLQ (Liquidity) too

If you're not used to these, you can get stopped out of some fantastic trades and deeply regret not knowing why.

Your question: expect price to pass through? in any timeframe? What works or doesnot on CP-ed area is widely discussed here already. Price Action applies to all timeframes. If you have troubles understanding compression, Go over all the posts in this HW section, Pay attention to words/corrections made by the seniors here, and watch CP webinar by IF. Then you may start doing the HW instructions (pay attention too to the instructions). This will take time, please do not expect to grasp just by skimming and looking at the posts. Learning by doing is best.:)
